subQuestions.questionText:
Grommets are used in the treatment of …
A deafness.
B blindness.
C middle-ear infection.
D multiple sclerosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Grommets are tiny tubes inserted through the tympanic membrane to drain fluid and equalise pressure, so they are used to treat middle-ear infection.

subQuestions.questionText:
The ability of the lens of the eye to change its shape when viewing an object that is near or far is called …
A binocular vision.
B accommodation.
C pupillary mechanism.
D refraction of light rays.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Accommodation is the ability of the lens to change its shape to focus on near or far objects.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is the visual defect that results from the uneven curvature of the cornea?
A Cataracts
B Long-sightedness
C Short-sightedness
D Astigmatism
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Astigmatism results from an uneven curvature of the cornea (or lens), causing light to be refracted unevenly and forming a blurred image.

subQuestions.questionText:
The receptor(s) involved in maintaining balance is/are the …
A organ of Corti only.
B maculae only.
C maculae and cristae only.
D organ of Corti, maculae and cristae.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Balance is maintained by the maculae (in the utricle and saccule) and the cristae (in the semi-circular canals). The organ of Corti is a receptor for hearing, not balance.

options.D: organ of Corti, maculae and cristae.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which of the following structures are involved in maintaining balance when there is a change in the direction of movement of the body?
A Semi-circular canals and cerebellum
B Eustachian tube and cerebellum
C Semi-circular canals and cerebrum
D Eustachian tube and cerebrum
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The semi-circular canals detect changes in the direction of movement, and the cerebellum coordinates balance and muscle movement.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which of the following structures are protected by the meninges?
A Spinal cord and receptors
B Spinal cord and brain
C Brain and effectors
D Effectors and receptors
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The meninges are the protective membranes that surround and protect the brain and spinal cord (the central nervous system).

subQuestions.questionText:
Two men were given a glucose-rich meal at the same time (0 hours). One man is diabetic and the other is non-diabetic. The diabetic did not receive any medical treatment. Their blood glucose levels were measured over a period of 3 hours. The graphs (W, X, Y and Z) show the possible blood glucose levels of the two men during this time. Which ONE of the graphs correctly represents the blood glucose levels of the two men?
A W
B X
C Y
D Z
(Refer to the graphs in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The correct graph shows the non-diabetic's blood glucose rising after the meal and then returning to normal (as insulin acts), while the untreated diabetic's blood glucose rises and remains high because insulin is not produced or is ineffective.

subQuestions.questionText:
During a reflex action, impulses enter the spinal cord by means of a/an …
A sensory neuron through the ventral root of the spinal nerve.
B sensory neuron through the dorsal root of the spinal nerve.
C interneuron through the ventral root of the spinal nerve.
D interneuron through the dorsal root of the spinal nerve.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
During a reflex action, impulses enter the spinal cord along the sensory neuron through the dorsal root of the spinal nerve.

options.A: sensory neuron through the ventral root of the spinal nerve.
options.B: sensory neuron through the dorsal root of the spinal nerve.
options.C: interneuron through the ventral root of the spinal nerve.
options.D: interneuron through the dorsal root of the spinal nerve.

subQuestions.questionText:
A person produces a smaller volume of urine most probably because …
A ADH levels are high in the blood and the renal tubules are more permeable to water.
B ADH levels are high in the blood and the renal tubules are less permeable to water.
C ADH levels are low in the blood and the renal tubules are more permeable to water.
D ADH levels are low in the blood and the renal tubules are less permeable to water.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
High ADH levels make the renal tubules more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood and a smaller volume of urine is produced.

options.A: ADH levels are high in the blood and the renal tubules are more permeable to water.
options.B: ADH levels are high in the blood and the renal tubules are less permeable to water.
options.C: ADH levels are low in the blood and the renal tubules are more permeable to water.
options.D: ADH levels are low in the blood and the renal tubules are less permeable to water.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The release of an ovum from the ovary.
subQuestions.memoText: Ovulation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The microscopic gap between two consecutive neurons.
subQuestions.memoText: Synapse (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The period of development of the foetus in the uterus.
subQuestions.memoText: Gestation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The growth movement of a plant in response to a stimulus.
subQuestions.memoText: Tropism (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The type of development in birds where the young are able to independently move and feed themselves after hatching.
subQuestions.memoText: Precocial development (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The extra-embryonic membrane that is responsible for the excretion of waste in an amniotic egg.
subQuestions.memoText: Allantois (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: Tubules in the testes where spermatogenesis occurs.
subQuestions.memoText: Seminiferous tubules (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The plant hormone that brings about seed dormancy when conditions are unfavourable.
subQuestions.memoText: Abscisic acid (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items.
Description (COLUMN I): An exocrine gland.
COLUMN II:
A: Cowper's gland
B: Pancreas
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Cowper's gland secretes its product through a duct (exocrine), and the pancreas is both exocrine (secretes digestive enzymes through a duct) and endocrine — so both act as exocrine glands.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items.
Description (COLUMN I): A component of the peripheral nervous system.
COLUMN II:
A: Cranial nerves
B: Spinal cord
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
Cranial nerves are part of the peripheral nervous system. The spinal cord is part of the central nervous system.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items.
Description (COLUMN I): A disorder of the nervous system characterised by the degeneration of the brain cells.
COLUMN II:
A: Goitre
B: Alzheimer's disease
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
Alzheimer's disease is a nervous-system disorder characterised by degeneration of brain cells. Goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland (endocrine), not a nervous-system disorder.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram shows the parts of the male reproductive system. Identify part:
(a) C
(b) F
(c) H
(Refer to the diagram of the male reproductive system in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) C – Vas deferens / sperm duct (1 mark)
(b) F – Scrotum (1 mark)
(c) H – Penis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the LETTER and NAME of the part that:
(a) Stores sperm temporarily
(b) Transports both semen and urine
(c) Produces testosterone
(Refer to the diagram of the male reproductive system in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) D – Epididymis (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)
(b) G – Urethra (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)
(c) E – Testis (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the LETTERS of TWO parts that contribute to the formation of semen.
(Refer to the diagram of the male reproductive system in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of: A, B, E (2 marks). Mark first TWO only.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram represents an ovum and a sperm. Identify part:
(a) B
(b) D
(c) H
(Refer to the diagram of the ovum and sperm in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B – Cytoplasm (1 mark)
(b) D – Jelly layer (1 mark)
(c) H – Tail / Flagellum (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the organelle found in large numbers in part G.
(Refer to the diagram of the ovum and sperm in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Mitochondrion (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the LETTERS of the TWO parts that fuse during fertilisation.
(Refer to the diagram of the ovum and sperm in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: A and F (2 marks). Mark first TWO only.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the meiotic process whereby ova are produced.
subQuestions.memoText: Oogenesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram represents a type of neuron found in the human body. Identify the type of neuron shown.
(Refer to the neuron diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Motor / efferent neuron (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Using the LETTERS A, B and C only, give the correct sequence for the transmission of an impulse along neuron 1.
(Refer to the neuron diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: C → B → A (2 marks). Must be in the correct sequence.

subQuestions.questionText:
Explain how the speed of transmission of impulses will differ for neuron 1 and neuron 2.
(Refer to the neuron diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- Impulses will be transmitted faster in neuron 1 / slower in neuron 2
- because of the presence of a myelin sheath in neuron 1 /
- absence of a myelin sheath in neuron 2

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why a person will feel the stimulus but will not be able to respond if only this type of neuron (the motor/efferent neuron) is damaged.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- Impulses from the receptor / sensory neuron
- will be transmitted to the central nervous system, but
- the impulse will not reach the effector

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram represents the structure of the human eye. Identify part C.
(Refer to the eye diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Choroid (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE function of part E.
(Refer to the eye diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark). Mark first ONE only:
- Holds the lens in position
- Connects the lens to the ciliary body
- Plays a role in accommodation

subQuestions.questionText:
State why the clearest image will form when light rays fall on part D.
(Refer to the eye diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Part D (the yellow spot / fovea) has the highest concentration of cones (1 mark).

subQuestions.questionText:
Explain ONE way in which part B is structurally different from part F.
(Refer to the eye diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(4 marks). Mark first ONE comparison only:
Option 1:
- Part B / sclera is opaque / does not allow light to pass through / white
- Part F / lens is transparent / allows light to pass into the eye
OR
Option 2:
- Part B / sclera is non-elastic / maintains the shape of the eye
- Part F / lens is elastic / able to change its shape

subQuestions.questionText:
Describe how the muscles in part A function to increase the amount of light entering the eye.
(Refer to the eye diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- The circular muscles relax
- The radial muscles contract
- causing the pupil to dilate

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how a blurred image forms if a person with normal vision wears spectacles with biconvex lenses while reading a book.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- The lenses in the spectacles will refract the light rays
- The lens of the eye also refracts the light rays
- The light rays will therefore be focused in front of the retina

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the extract: Endometriosis is a medical condition that occurs when the endometrium develops in or on other structures such as the Fallopian tubes, ovaries or pelvis. It is caused by higher than normal levels of oestrogen. Females with this condition will most likely experience mild to severe menstrual pains, and it can sometimes lead to infertility. Doctors may prescribe a contraceptive pill (containing progesterone) as treatment to reduce the development of the endometrium.
Name the structure where the endometrium normally develops.
subQuestions.memoText: Uterus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Endometriosis occurs when the endometrium develops in or on other structures such as the Fallopian tubes. Explain why endometriosis in the Fallopian tubes may lead to infertility.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- The thickened layer may cause an obstruction / blockage
- which may prevent the passage of gametes
- preventing fertilisation from taking place
OR
- The thickened layer may cause an obstruction / blockage
- which may prevent the embryo from reaching the uterus / implantation could occur in the Fallopian tube
- which may lead to the death of the embryo / rupturing of the Fallopian tube / miscarriage

subQuestions.questionText: Doctors may prescribe a contraceptive pill containing progesterone to reduce the development of the endometrium in a female with endometriosis. Use the negative feedback mechanism to explain why the pills containing progesterone are successful in treating endometriosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
(4 marks)
- A high concentration of progesterone
- inhibits the pituitary gland from secreting FSH
- Without FSH a follicle will not develop in the ovary
- Therefore, oestrogen will not be secreted

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of hearing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 7 of the following (7 marks):
- The pinna of the ear traps sound waves
- The auditory canal directs the sound waves to the tympanic membrane
- causing the tympanic membrane to vibrate
- which causes the ossicles to vibrate and
- pass the vibrations to the oval window / amplify the vibrations
- (Pressure) waves are set up in the inner ear / perilymph / endolymph
- The organ of Corti is stimulated
- and converts the stimuli into impulses
- which are transmitted by the auditory nerve
- to the cerebrum for interpretation

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram shows a developing human foetus. Identify part D.
(Refer to the foetus diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Chorion (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State TWO functions of the fluid in part C.
(Refer to the foetus diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Acts as a shock absorber
- It prevents desiccation / dehydration
- It helps to keep the temperature within a narrow range
- It facilitates free movement of the foetus

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the development of the zygote until implantation occurs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 of the following (4 marks):
- The zygote divides by mitosis
- to form a (solid) ball of cells
- called the morula
- which develops into a hollow ball of cells
- called the blastula / blastocyst

subQuestions.questionText:
State TWO ways in which part A functions in protecting the developing foetus.
(Refer to the foetus diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Acts as a micro-filter / protects against pathogens
- Removal of harmful metabolic waste
- Produces antibodies
- Maintains the endometrium

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify blood vessel B.
(Refer to the foetus diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Umbilical vein (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the nutrition of a human foetus differs from that of oviparous organisms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 of the following (3 marks):
- In humans the developing foetus receives nutrients from the mother's blood
- via the placenta / umbilical vein
- In oviparous organisms the developing embryo receives nutrients from the yolk / albumen

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams show the human brain and the human kidney. Identify part A.
(Refer to the diagram of the human brain and kidney in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Cerebellum (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State ONE function of part C.
(Refer to the diagram of the human brain and kidney in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark). Mark first ONE only:
- Connects the two hemispheres of the brain
- Allows for communication between the two hemispheres of the brain

subQuestions.questionText:
A person sustained a head injury in a car accident and lost his memory. Write down the LETTER and NAME of the part of the brain that was affected.
(Refer to the diagram of the human brain and kidney in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: D – Cerebrum (2 marks: 1 for letter, 1 for name)

subQuestions.questionText:
During an emergency situation, gland E releases a hormone that prepares the body for a 'fight or flight' response by stimulating an increase in breathing rate and heart rate. This increase leads to increased energy production in the skeletal muscles and an increase in blood carbon dioxide levels.
(a) Name the hormone secreted by gland E in an emergency situation. (1)
(b) Explain how an increase in breathing rate and heart rate results in increased energy production in skeletal muscles. (4)
(c) Describe how part B is involved in carbon dioxide homeostasis. (4)
(Refer to the diagram of the human brain and kidney in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Adrenalin (1 mark)

(b) (4 marks)
- More air / oxygen will be inhaled
- Blood will be pumped faster
- therefore, transporting more oxygen and glucose to the skeletal muscles
- which will increase the rate of cellular respiration / metabolism

(c) Any 4 of the following (4 marks):
- Part B / the medulla oblongata is stimulated
- and sends impulses to the heart and to
- the breathing muscles / intercostal muscles and diaphragm
- More blood is transported to the lungs
- and the carbon dioxide is exhaled faster
- and the carbon dioxide levels return to normal

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows the average rate of blood flow to the skin at different environmental temperatures.
Environmental temperature (°C) | Average rate of blood flow to the skin (mℓ/100 mℓ tissue/min)
0 | 2,5
5 | 4
20 | 4,5
35 | 11
45 | 18
50 | 19
Give the environmental temperature at which there was the greatest average rate of blood flow to the skin.
subQuestions.memoText: 50 °C (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Using the data in the table below, describe the relationship between the environmental temperature and the average rate of blood flow to the skin.
Environmental temperature (°C) | Average rate of blood flow to the skin (mℓ/100 mℓ tissue/min)
0 | 2,5
5 | 4
20 | 4,5
35 | 11
45 | 18
50 | 19
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
As the (environmental) temperature increases, the average rate of blood flow to the skin increases.

subQuestions.questionText:
Using the data in the table, calculate the percentage increase in blood flow to the skin between 5 °C and 35 °C. Show ALL your workings.
Environmental temperature (°C) | Average rate of blood flow to the skin (mℓ/100 mℓ tissue/min)
0 | 2,5
5 | 4
20 | 4,5
35 | 11
45 | 18
50 | 19

Explain the average rate of blood flow to the skin between 20 °C and 45 °C.
Environmental temperature (°C) | Average rate of blood flow to the skin (mℓ/100 mℓ tissue/min)
0 | 2,5
5 | 4
20 | 4,5
35 | 11
45 | 18
50 | 19
subQuestions.memoText:
(4 marks)
- As the temperature increases from 20 °C to 45 °C
- vasodilation occurs / blood vessels dilate
- to increase the rate of blood flow / more blood flows to the skin
- so that more heat / sweat can be lost

subQuestions.questionText:
Frostbite is a condition where long-term exposure to extremely cold conditions (0 °C or less) leads to the death of tissue in areas like the hands and feet. Use the data from the table to explain why tissue may die.
Environmental temperature (°C) | Average rate of blood flow to the skin (mℓ/100 mℓ tissue/min)
0 | 2,5
5 | 4
20 | 4,5
35 | 11
45 | 18
50 | 19
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
- Less blood flows to the skin at low temperatures
- Less oxygen / nutrients reach the cells of the tissue and the cells may die
OR
- Less blood flows to the skin at low temperatures
- More carbon dioxide / waste products accumulate in the cells of the tissue and the cells may die

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the negative feedback mechanism that occurs when thyroxin levels in the blood are high.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks)
- The pituitary gland is stimulated
- to secrete less TSH
- Low TSH levels cause the thyroid gland
- to secrete less thyroxin
- Thyroxin levels return to normal

subQuestions.questionText: A person has a medical condition that results in the under-secretion of thyroxin. Explain why this person will gain weight if the thyroxin levels remain continuously low in the blood.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- The rate of metabolism / respiration in the body decreases
- Less glucose will be broken down
- and more glucose will be converted and stored as fat / glycogen

subQuestions.questionText:
A group of learners conducted an investigation to determine the effect of auxins on the growth of stems in bean seedlings. Procedure: 30 bean seeds were germinated for 5 days to produce seedlings. The seedlings were divided into 3 groups (A, B and C) of 10 seedlings each. The tips of all the seedlings were cut at the same length. In group A, the cut tip was placed back on top of the young stem. In group B, the tip was not placed back. In group C, a piece of plastic was placed on top of the cut surface and the tip was then placed on top of the plastic. All groups were placed in a dark cupboard for a week and the growth of the stem was observed.
Identify the dependent variable in this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Stem growth (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In the investigation on the effect of auxins on stem growth in bean seedlings, the tips of the young stems were cut. Why did the learners cut the tips of the young stems?
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
- To remove the source of auxins
- The tip produces auxins

subQuestions.questionText: In the investigation, the seedlings were divided into 3 groups of 10 seedlings each. Give ONE reason why 10 bean seedlings were used in each group.
subQuestions.memoText: To increase the reliability / validity of the results (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In the investigation: group A had the cut tip placed back on the young stem; group B had the tip not placed back; group C had a piece of plastic placed on the cut surface with the tip on top of the plastic. Write down the LETTER(S) (A, B or C) of the group(s) where there will be no upward growth of the stem.
subQuestions.memoText:
B and C (2 marks)
In B the auxin source (tip) was removed; in C the plastic prevents auxins from the tip diffusing into the stem — so no auxins reach the stem and there is no upward growth.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how auxins cause apical dominance.
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks)
- The presence of auxins in the tip of the stem
- stimulate upward growth
- and inhibit the development of lateral branches

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the plant hormone:
(a) Other than auxins, that promotes the germination of seeds
(b) That inhibits the germination of seeds
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Gibberellins (1 mark)
(b) Abscisic acid (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the extract: The bluefin tuna, the great white shark and the bottlenose dolphin are three aquatic species found in the Indian Ocean. An adult bluefin tuna releases up to 540 000 000 eggs into the water annually (external fertilisation), while the great white shark female produces 2 to 12 offspring through ovovivipary every two years. A bottlenose dolphin female, being a mammal, is viviparous and produces one offspring every two to three years.
Name the type of fertilisation that takes place in the bottlenose dolphin.
subQuestions.memoText: Internal fertilisation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The great white shark female produces 2 to 12 offspring through ovovivipary every two years. Explain how TWO of the reproductive strategies of the great white shark increase its reproductive success.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following pairs (2 x 2 = 4 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Internal fertilisation (1) increases the chances of fertilisation (1)
- Ovovivipary / eggs retained inside the female's body (1) where they are protected (1)

subQuestions.questionText: An adult bluefin tuna releases up to 540 000 000 eggs into the water annually. Explain ONE reason why the bluefin tuna releases a large number of eggs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following pairs (2 marks):
- To increase the chances of fertilisation / the survival of the eggs / number of offspring
- As eggs may be lost to predators / environmental factors
- Since there is external fertilisation
